chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, and Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān, all together from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, who said:

“Maintain the proper sequence in wudu (ablution) as Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said: begin with the face, then the two hands, then wipe the head and the feet. Do not put anything before something else, thereby opposing what you have been commanded to do. If you wash the forearm before the face, then begin with the face and repeat over the forearm. And if you wipe the foot before the head, then wipe over the head before the foot, then repeat over the foot. Begin with what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, began with.”

key_terms.أُمِرْتَ: you were commanded, referring to the divinely prescribed order
key_terms.الذِّرَاعَ: the forearm/arm, mentioned in the case of performing the washing out of sequence
key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, which is to be wiped after washing the face and hands
key_terms.الرِّجْلَيْنِ: the feet, which are to be wiped after the head
key_terms.الْوَجْهِ: the face, the first obligatory part to wash in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification being described
key_terms.الْيَدَيْنِ: the two hands/arms, washed after the face in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order of actions in wudu (ablution), and what should be done if the order is broken?
ai.summary: This hadith states the obligation of maintaining the prescribed order in wudu (ablution): face, hands, then wiping the head and feet. It instructs that if the order is violated, the earlier misplaced act must be redone in its proper sequence. The report is significant in Shia fiqh as evidence for tartīb, the required sequence of acts in wudu (ablution).
